scenario: AITA for 'stealing' my Dad's business idea and making a success of it? | Title says it all really. I (26M) technically ''stole'' my dad's business idea. When I first heard it from him, it was so simple yet so...genius. I can't say exactly what it is here, but it was genius. The thing is, me and my dad (55M) are complete opposites. He's the more introverted and quiet type. He's always been *very* intelligent, but he's lacked the ability to *get things done.* I've been told I'm more like my grandad (75M, my dad's dad). Physically, I look more like my grandad, but personality wise, I guess I'm a bit more impulsive and hot headed and not as intelligent as my dad, but I get things done. Perhaps I'm more ''traditional masculine'' than my dad. Its like I should be in the older generation, and he should be from the newer one. When I heard my Dad's business idea, I was amazed, but I didn't truly believe my Dad could pull it off. He doesn't get things done. He's always been full of great ideas, but ideas not put to use are useless. So I took the idea and ran with it. I got IP rights and started the business with it 2 years ago. Since then, its been a massive success. Not millions or anything, but into the six figures and the potential to make millions is there perhaps in the next half decade if things keep going well. My dad was very upset when I did this, but didn't say much. I could tell by his facial expressions. My mom (55F) said I've done her proud and done the right thing. Well I confronted my dad yesterday to ask him how he feels and he said I'm a ''fucking asshole''. He said he felt betrayed by me and nearly started crying. I told him straight, ''You've always been a man of ideas, but I'm a man of action''. Then my sister (28F) walks in and starts saying shit to me, defending my dad. Both my mom and granddad have taken my side. I even offered my dad 20% of all profits, but he rejected and told me to get out. I understand why he's upset, but I think he's being unreasonable here. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing by taking my dad's business idea and running with it. Let me start by understanding the situation better. My dad came up with this idea that seemed really simple but genius. I remember when he first told me about it; I was amazed. But then, I didn't think he could actually make it work because he's more of an ideas person, not so much into executing them. So, I decided to take that idea and turn it into a business. I got the IP rights and started the company two years ago. It's been a massive success, making six figures and with the potential to make millions in the next few years. But here's the thing: my dad was really upset when I did this. He didn't say much at first, but I could tell by his facial expressions that he was hurt. My mom, on the other hand, was proud of me and thought I did the right thing. I even confronted my dad about how he felt, and he called me a "fucking asshole," saying he felt betrayed. I told him that he's a man of ideas, and I'm a man of action. My sister walked in and started defending my dad, but both my mom and granddad are on my side. I even offered my dad 20% of all profits, but he rejected it and told me to get out. I understand why he's upset, but I think he's being unreasonable. I mean, I took his idea and made it successful when he couldn't. Shouldn't he be proud of me for taking his idea and turning it into something real? Or is it wrong for me to take his idea without his permission? Maybe I should think about the concept of ownership. Did I steal his idea, or did I just take it and make it work? If he couldn't execute it, does that mean the idea was just sitting there unused? By taking it and making it successful, am I not doing him a favor? Or is it more about the emotional aspect of feeling betrayed? Also, there's the issue of family dynamics. My dad and I are complete opposites. He's introverted and quiet, while I'm more impulsive and get things done. Maybe he feels that I took something that was his, and by doing so, I've taken away his chance to prove himself. Even though I offered him a share of the profits, he rejected it, which might indicate that it's not about the money but about the principle of me taking his idea. I wonder if there's a middle ground here. Could we have discussed the idea first before I took action? Maybe if I had talked to him about it and asked for his permission or partnership, he wouldn't have felt so betrayed. But I didn't do that; I just went ahead and did it on my own. On the other hand, I made the business successful, which benefits not just me but potentially the whole family in the long run. My mom and granddad support me, which is a good sign. But my dad's reaction is really strong, and it's affecting our relationship. I also need to consider the legal aspect. I got the IP rights, which means I legally own the idea now. But does that override the emotional or familial claim my dad might have on it? It seems like a complicated situation with both legal and emotional dimensions. Maybe I should reflect on what's important in a family. Is it about supporting each other's ideas and working together, or is it about individual achievements? It seems like my dad values the idea as his own creation, while I value the execution and success of it. I also need to think about how this will affect our family moving forward. If I continue without reconciling with my dad, it might create long-term issues. But if I give him a share or try to make amends, it might help mend our relationship. In the end, I think I did what I thought was right by taking the idea and making it successful, but I can see why my dad feels betrayed. It's a tough situation where both sides have valid points. Maybe the best approach is to find a way to reconcile our differences and move forward together, even if it means making some compromises.
